title: Public Corporations and Government Undertakings — Control, Autonomy and Accountability

content.overview: Public corporations and government undertakings are instruments of state economic and social policy. They combine commercial form with public control. Courts examine when such bodies are 'State' under Article 12, the intensity of judicial review over their actions, and the statutory controls applicable to them.
content.glance: Identify the body's legal form and control structure; test whether it is 'State' under Article 12; determine the applicable review standard; and match the appropriate public-law or private-law remedy.
content.study: Public corporations are created by or under statute or by executive action to perform commercial or developmental functions. Whether their actions attract public-law remedies depends largely on whether they fall within 'State' under Article 12 — typically through tests of deep and pervasive control, public function, and governmental character. Employment, contract and regulatory disputes may attract different intensities of review. Statutory control mechanisms coexist with judicial review. Current-law framing: ground the analysis in the Constitution and the specific statute. Do not treat BSA 2023 as the source of this doctrine.

sections.heading: Nature and Purpose
sections.body: Public corporations pursue public purposes through corporate form, combining operational flexibility with public accountability.

sections.heading: Article 12 and State
sections.body: Deep and pervasive control, public function and governmental character help determine whether the body is State for fundamental-rights purposes.

sections.heading: Control and Accountability
sections.body: Statutory directions, audit, legislative oversight and judicial review structure control over public corporations.

sections.heading: Judicial Review Intensity
sections.body: Commercial decisions may attract lighter review than regulatory or monopoly functions, but arbitrariness remains reviewable where Article 12 applies.

sections.heading: Remedies
sections.body: Writs under Articles 32/226, statutory appeals and private-law actions may all be relevant depending on the character of the dispute.

examples.title: Instrumentality test
examples.body: A government-controlled corporation exercises deep and pervasive governmental control and performs public functions. Article 12 analysis is engaged.

examples.title: Pure commercial dispute
examples.body: A purely commercial contract dispute with a public corporation may attract private-law remedies; public-law intensity depends on the function and control structure.

hypotheticals.question: Is every government company automatically State under Article 12?
hypotheticals.analysis: No. Article 12 requires a functional and control analysis; form alone is not conclusive.

hypotheticals.question: Are commercial decisions of public corporations never reviewable?
hypotheticals.analysis: Arbitrariness and statutory breaches remain reviewable where public-law standards apply.

cases.name: Praga Tools Corporation v C.A. Imanual
cases.facts: Whether a public-sector corporation was amenable to writ jurisdiction.
cases.issue: When can a public corporation be subjected to public-law remedies?
cases.ratioDecidendi: A writ may issue where a public authority has a public duty; the precise remedy depends on the nature of the duty.
cases.holding: The Court explained the limits of writ relief against a company.
cases.relevance: Authority already present in the topic file.

cases.name: Sukhdev Singh v Bhagatram Sardar Singh Raghuvanshi
cases.facts: Status of statutory corporations under Article 12.
cases.issue: When can statutory corporations be treated as instrumentalities of the State?
cases.ratioDecidendi: Statutory corporations exercising public functions may fall within State and are subject to fundamental-rights constraints.
cases.holding: Named statutory corporations treated as State instrumentalities.
cases.relevance: Authority already present in the topic file.

cases.name: Ajay Hasia v Khalid Mujib Sehravardi
cases.facts: Whether a society managing a college was an instrumentality of government.
cases.issue: What factors determine whether an entity is an instrumentality of the State?
cases.ratioDecidendi: Article 12 turns on the substance of governmental control and functional character rather than corporate form alone.
cases.holding: The Court articulated indicia for determining State agency.

questionsAndAnswers.question: How should a public-corporation problem be analysed?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: I. Identify legal form and control. II. Apply Article 12 tests. III. Determine review intensity. IV. Match public or private remedy.

questionsAndAnswers.question: What should submissions contain?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: Control structure; Article 12 analysis; function character; precise relief.
